== Biography ==

The Queen is the sovereign ruler of Wonderland, a figure of absolute authority whose word is law and whose displeasure carries the threat of immediate execution. She is known throughout the realm for her violent temperament and her freely dispensed death sentences, which she announces with the refrain "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" She orders these executions with such frequency and casual brutality that those around her live in constant dread of offending her, knowing that any moment might bring a fatal judgment.

The Queen's most notable display of her volatile nature occurs during a croquet game, where she becomes "in a furious passion" and goes "stamping about, and shouting 'Off with his head!' or 'Off with her head!' about once in a minute." The chaotic nature of her court proceedings—where rules are neither clear nor consistently observed—reflects her absolute power and capricious will. Her subjects include those in her employ, such as various members of her court, and she commands both the respect and fear of those who inhabit Wonderland.

She is remembered in waking life through the impressions she leaves upon those who encounter her realm. Her "shrill voice" ordering "off her unfortunate guests to execution" echoes even in the dreams of those who have left Wonderland behind, a persistent reminder of her merciless authority and the constant peril that defines her kingdom.

== Narrative role ==

The Queen is the volatile sovereign of Wonderland, known for her explosive temper and swift judgments. She first enters the story when Alice receives an invitation to a croquet party at her grounds. The Hatter later recounts a fateful encounter: during a Queen of Hearts concert the previous March, he quarreled with Time itself, and the Queen, outraged that he was murdering the time by singing badly, bawled out "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!" and condemned him to death—a sentence that left him frozen at six o'clock ever since.

When Alice arrives at the Queen's croquet ground, she witnesses the chaotic nature of the Queen's domain. Three gardeners are frantically painting white roses red to conceal a mistake before the Queen discovers it. The Queen's grand procession arrives with soldiers, courtiers, royal children, and various guests, including the White Rabbit. Alice refuses to lie flat in deference during the procession and speaks boldly when questioned, prompting the Queen to order her beheading. The King intervenes to spare Alice, but the Queen swiftly turns her wrath upon the gardeners, ordering their execution after discovering their paint-stained roses.

Alice is then invited by the Queen to play croquet—a game that proves as chaotic and violent as the Queen herself. During play, the Queen enters a furious passion, stamping about and shouting "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!" about once in a minute, creating an atmosphere of constant mortal peril. Alice is escorted by the Queen back to the croquet ground, where the Queen executes most of the other players, sparing only the King and Alice herself. When the Queen later confronts the Duchess, she threatens her with execution, and the Duchess flees immediately.

The Queen presides over the trial of the Knave of Hearts, accused of stealing tarts made by the Queen of Hearts. During these proceedings, she threatens the Hatter with execution while reading a list of singers, causing him to flee the court in terror. She orders the Dormouse's removal from the court when he answers a question out of turn. Throughout the trial, the Queen, along with the King and jury, attempts to interpret evidence, each finding meanings that seem to support predetermined conclusions about the Knave's guilt. When Alice finally declares the court nothing but a pack of cards and defies the Queen's orders, the card-creatures—including the Queen—fly at her and disperse into the air.

== Personality ==

The Queen is a figure of sudden and violent passion, prone to outbursts of fury that erupt without warning or apparent cause. When the Hatter sang during a tea gathering, she reacted by leaping up and crying out "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!"—a response so disproportionate that even those present found it "dreadfully savage." Her temper is not a fleeting mood but a defining characteristic: during a croquet match, she entered "a furious passion" and spent the game stamping about the ground, shouting threats of beheading at a rate of once per minute, whether the provocation warranted it or not.

The Queen exercises absolute, unquestioning authority in Wonderland. Her word is law, and her preferred instrument of governance is the death sentence—so freely dispensed that one observer marvels at the fact that anyone remains alive in her realm at all. She shows no patience for incompetence, disorder, or contradiction. When roses were painted the wrong colour, she was clearly someone to be feared; when gardeners and courtiers fail to anticipate her wishes, they meet with her wrath.

Her voice is distinctive: shrill and commanding, it cuts through the chaos of her court as she orders unfortunate guests to execution. Those who encounter her learn quickly that her favour is precarious and her displeasure swift. She does not negotiate, explain, or show mercy; she simply commands and expects obedience. The very sound of her name—her "shrill voice ordering off her unfortunate guests"—became, in memory, almost synonymous with the arbitrary cruelty of Wonderland itself.

== Powers ==

The Queen is the monarch of Wonderland, a figure of volatile authority whose word is law—or at least, the law as she understands it in any given moment. She is prone to fits of fury and has made execution by beheading her characteristic response to perceived slights or failures. During a game of croquet, when the Hatter began to sing and murdered a verse of "Twinkle, Twinkle," she jumped up and bawled out, "He's murdering the time! Off with his head!" Her outbursts are frequent and terrible: during the croquet game itself, she was soon "in a furious passion, and went stamping about, and shouting 'Off with his head!' or 'Off with her head!' about once in a minute."

In the minds of Wonderland's inhabitants, the Queen's court is defined by her appetite for bloodshed. Those around her believe that "they're dreadfully fond of beheading people here; the great wonder is, that there's any one left alive!" Her commands carry the weight of absolute authority: she orders the Dormouse to be collared and beheaded, and her "shrill voice" rings out ordering her unfortunate guests to execution. Yet beneath the terror she inspires lies an oddly whimsical logic—her threats and rages follow the strange dream-reasoning of Wonderland itself, where rage subsides as quickly as it rises and the next moment may bring an entirely different passion.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — enemy. Alice's defiance and growth provoke the Queen's wrath, and the Queen orders her beheading; their opposition seems rooted in Alice's refusal to submit to Wonderland's illogical authority.

'''[[Dormouse]]''' — enemy. The Queen shrieks commands to collar, behead, and turn the Dormouse out of court, marking the creature as one of her frequent targets for execution.

'''[[Hatter]]''' — enemy. The Hatter incurs the Queen's anger when he is perceived to be "murdering the time" during a song, prompting her to demand his beheading.

'''[[White Rabbit]]''' — employment. The White Rabbit serves in the Queen's court and carries out her will, appearing in her procession and assisting in her proceedings.

'''[[Gryphon]]''' — employment. The Gryphon serves under the Queen's authority in Wonderland.

== Trivia ==

* The Queen's most frequent command is "Off with his head!" or "Off with her head!", which she shouts approximately once per minute during moments of agitation.
* Her authority extends to the organization of leisure activities in Wonderland, including the croquet games played on her grounds with living creatures as implements.
* The Queen's household appears to include employed courtiers and attendants, from the White Rabbit to various guardians of her court.
* Those who have encountered her regard her disposition as "dreadfully savage", and her capacity for sudden violent outbursts is well-known enough that even visitors to Wonderland live in fear of incurring her displeasure.
